items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name. Pulled the record by email and addressed him as 'sir' roughly forty times across a 26-minute call. The customer had to ask twice for the REP's name in the first four lines.
No 'how are you today?' and no agenda statement of any kind - never said what the call would cover or how long it would take, and never asked 'sound good?'

Date availability was handled chaotically. Told the customer Thursday was booked, offered Friday the 21st, then said 'we won't be able to do that,' then said the 21st was available, then said the 19th 'has already been taken just right now.' The customer said outright 'You read them too quickly' and had to ask him to repeat the list.
Never confirmed origin or destination address or zip code, even though he was building a trip-fee-relevant estimate.
Never asked about stairs at the origin, on a two-story house where the customer volunteered that the bathroom being packed was upstairs.
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops.

No moving-stressor question. Said 'I don't want you to be stressed' but never asked what the customer was worried about, on a call where the customer said four separate times he was still trying to figure things out.
No 'pricing is super simple' framing and no what's-included list - never said gas, truck, taxes, insurance, pads, bands, or tools are in the rate.

No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned, on a move containing 100-year-old books, an antique tea cart, crystal, porcelain figurines, and artwork. The customer used the word 'fragile' himself and the rep replied 'of course, of course, of course.'
No 'no hidden fees' pitch - no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees.

Entire Clock section skipped: never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, never gave the 2.5 hour minimum, never explained 15-minute prorated increments. Quoted $210/hr flat and an eight-hour budget with no clock mechanics behind it.

No Save Your Ass prep speech. No consolidation examples and no carload tip - and the customer explicitly said he had been collecting open-top boxes 'that someone could carry out to the car,' which is the exact opening for the carload tip.
Never mentioned that no deposit is required, on a call where the customer's only stated objection was that he wasn't ready to commit and there was one truck left.
Email handoff never clearly explained. The only reference is a cut-off 'then I'll just send you' - no confirmation email, no bolded detail list, no reply-with-corrections ask.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave office hours or how to reach the branch.
No Ecobox referral, on a call where the customer asked directly what box sizes Einstein offers and was told 'we don't provide boxes sir, you have to go to our branch to buy boxes.'
No insurance explanation of any kind - neither the $2,000 No Worries coverage nor the 60 cents per pound baseline.
top_strength: Genuinely strong estimate construction under bad conditions. The customer could not tell him what he was moving - he changed the inventory a dozen times over 26 minutes - and Arden still built a defensible number by breaking it into two hours of packing plus five hours of wrap/load/unload, then explicitly adding an hour for the sixth-floor elevator and the long walk from the loading dock, and saying out loud 'just to be safe that we're not under quoted.' He also handled the ambiguity well by asking for photos so the estimate could be corrected before move day, and he was patient about it: 'It's okay sir. Go ahead, part of my job sir.'
coaching_note: Arden built a good estimate and then never sold it. He hit zero of the four differentiators, skipped the entire Clock section, and never said 'no deposit' - on a call where the customer's only hesitation was commitment and there was one truck left for the 21st. Next call: after you give the number, run the fixed close every time - clock mechanics, No Worries $2,000, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, then 'there's no deposit to hold it, want me to lock that truck in?' Also get and use the customer's name; 'sir' forty times is not the same thing.
phone_presence_notes: Real patience and warmth in spots ('part of my job sir', 'of course, of course'), and the customer stayed positive, but the delivery was hard to follow - the customer asked him to repeat himself four separate times and told him directly he was reading too quickly - and zero name use kept it transactional.
audio_review_reason: Customer explicitly said 'You read them too quickly' and asked for repeats four times. Pace and clarity are audio attributes the transcript can only hint at - worth verifying before coaching him on it.
